title: weight-hot-reload-scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Problem: iterating on model weights (quantization adjustments, small finetunes, delta patches) in private/Dedicated deployments is slow and risky. Full redeploys are heavy: cold-start latency, cache misses, state loss for active sessions, and long turnaround for dev feedback loops.

Idea (high level):
- Provide a developer-first "weight hot-reload" flow that lets engineers push small weight deltas or alternate weight shards and have the serving runtime apply them in-place with minimal disruption.
- Support two modes: 
  1) ephemeral dev mode: single-node local/VPC sandbox where weight swap is immediate and sessions auto-migrate to new params;
  2) staged rollout: canary subset of workers serve new weights, traffic gradually shifts, with fallback to previous weights on regressions.

Goals / success signals:
- iteration time for weight tweaks drops from hours -> minutes for dev sandbox flows
- production canary rollouts complete in <10 minutes for small weight swaps (non-architectural changes)
- zero or bounded increase in p95 latency (<10% overhead) during swap
- session continuity preserved for in-flight requests where possible, otherwise graceful fallback with clear errors

User stories:
- as an applied-ml engineer, I want to push a delta quantization profile and smoke-test it against a small set of requests without restarting the fleet
- as an infra owner, I want the server to verify compatibility (arch, tokenizer, kv-cache layout) before applying weights so we don't corrupt state
- as an SRE, I want a one-command rollback that restores the previous weight set if eval metrics degrade
- as a product engineer, I want to run A/B comparisons between two weight sets on the same request distribution and collect perf/quality metrics

Acceptance criteria (rough):
- weighted swap workflow exists in CLI and Console: upload artifact, run dry-run (compat check), apply to dev worker or create canary group
- runtime supports layered weight tables: base weights + delta overlays; overlay can be applied/unapplied atomically per-layer or per-shard
- metric hooks emit reload events, swap duration, errored shard list, and per-host health check
- rollback path re-applies previous overlay and verifies checksums

Technical sketch / constraints:
- weight artifacts: tar.gz containing metadata (model-id, arch hash, tokenizer hash, layer-shard manifests, checksum) and binary shards. Small deltas are encouraged (weight diff files) to reduce transfer.
- compatibility checks: architecture match (num layers, dims), KV cache layout, tokenization; fail with actionable messages if mismatch
- swap mechanism: for GPU workers, copy new shard into GPU-visible storage (NVRAM or local SSD), update memory map pointers, warm a tiny subset of layers to populate caches, then flip pointer atomically. If atomic pointer flip not possible, coordinate quiesce windows per worker to drain in-flight requests (short pause <100ms preferred).
- session handling: option A = keep existing sessions bound to old weights until they finish; option B = migrate sessions by replaying recent context onto new weights (costly). Start with option A + sticky affinity for in-flight sessions, with migration experiment later.
- fallback: maintain previous shards on host until new weights validated and checkpointed; ensure a robust rollback that doesn't rely on global orchestration if individual hosts fail

Metrics to capture:
- swap_time_per_host_ms, swap_success_rate, p50/p95 latency pre/post swap, model-accuracy/regression signals on eval-set, cache-warmup-token-count, on-disk transfer bytes, CPU/GPU memory delta

Console/CLI UX notes:
- "redwood weights push --model X --artifact foo.tgz --mode dev" -> returns list of target hosts, dry-run compatibility output, estimated transfer size
- Console: drag-drop artifact, run dry-run, select canary group slider (1%-50%), auto-attach evaluation prompt-set, toggle auto-rollback on metric thresholds

Experiments / MVP plan (3 phases):
- MVP (dev-only): local sandbox + single-host hot-swap for weights. No canary. Provide CLI + logs. Focus on developer cycle time and basic safety checks.
- Phase 2 (canary): support canary grouping, measurement collection, auto-rollback policy. Surface in Console.
- Phase 3 (production multi-host): coordinated swap protocol, layered overlays, session migration experiments, cross-region strategies.

Risks / unknowns:
- atomic pointer flips for GPU memory mapping may not be possible with some runtimes (CUDA driver constraints). Need to prototype on current runtime and fallback to short quiesce windows.
- large weight transfer costs on Dedicated networks; need delta encoding and shard prefetching
- compatibility verification must be exhaustive or we risk silent corruption of KV cache, positional embeddings mismatch, etc.

Open questions:
- what is the minimum subset of layers we can reasonably swap live without retraining? (embedding layers vs attention vs FFN)
- can we leverage focused fine-tune deltas (LoRA-style) to minimize binary size and simplify overlays?
- how to surface per-session weight provenance in audit logs for compliance?

Integration/deps:
- storage: leverage existing shard store (S3-compatible or GCS) + local SSD cache
- orchestration: integrate with rollout controller (A/B, canary) in Platform layer
- console: new artifact UI + metric binding to eval prompt-set
- security: artifact signing (SigV4 + internal sig) and optional KMS encryption for private deployments

Prototype tasks (next 2 weeks):
- quick spike: implement a minimal weight overlay loader in the dev runtime (extract shard, mmap into process, flip pointer) — measure downtime
- CLI stub for push/dry-run/apply for local sandbox
- create tiny eval harness (20 prompts) that compares responses, reports diffs and latency changes

Notes to self / todo:
- sync with Arjun on mmap feasibility and GPU driver constraints (ask about CUDA driver memory remap capabilities)
- sketch data model for artifact metadata (manifest fields we want)
- find 3 candidate models to test (small -> medium) and measure transfer times
- check with security about signing/encryption for private deploy artifacts

Random thoughts / heuristics:
- encourage LoRA/delta-first workflows; present recommended delta size targets in Console
- if swap time > 2s per host, prefer canary shifting rather than immediate fleet swap
- provide "staging pool" of warm hosts that prefetch artifacts to accelerate rollouts

End of notes.
mini_summary: Scratchpad exploring a hot-reload flow for swapping model weight artifacts in-place to speed dev iteration and enable fast canary rollouts. Includes user stories, acceptance criteria, technical constraints, metrics, and an MVP roadmap.
